title: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review - Summit Clinic
summary: Review of Redwood's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 posture, access to trust center artifacts, controls mapping for PHI handling, encryption/KMS options, audit/logging retention, and next steps for providing reports and a controls matrix.
topics: Trust Center access and portal read-only links
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
Encryption at rest/in-transit and KMS/HSM options
Audit logs, retention and SIEM integration
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're just gonna do a quick SOC two / ISO twenty seven review, make sure you all have what you need. Maya, thanks for taking the time.
[00:12] Maya: Yeah, thanks Alex, appreciate it. We are short on time today, we've got a few specific asks: we need the latest SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert scope, and a controls mapping for HIPAA since we handle PHI. Also clarity on logs and KMS.
[00:28] Alex: Totally, we'll cover all that. Priya's gonna walk through the technical controls and where the artifacts live in the trust center. Priya?
[00:34] Priya: Thanks. So quick agenda, I'll show where the SOC 2 report sits, what the ISO scope includes, then go deeper on encryption, RBAC/SSO and audit logs. There may be a couple of minute pauses while I pull up references.
[00:48] Tom: Quick question up front — does Redwood host PHI in the hosted offering? And if so, what's the recommended deployment mode?
[00:56] Priya: Great question. For PHI we usually recommend either Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted is possible but we'd need a contractual addendum and we typically advise customers to use Dedicated for guaranteed isolation. Our Private option can be VPC peered or on-prem, depending on network needs.
[01:12] Sana: When you say Dedicated, is that physical isolation or logical?
[01:16] Priya: It's tenant-isolated GPU pools — dedicated capacity. Not necessarily single-tenant hardware by default, but the workloads are in reserved pools with strict network controls and no cross-tenant data plane. For full hardware separation we can discuss a private on-prem package.
[01:30] Maya: Okay, good. Next — SOC 2. Do you have a current Type II report and when is the coverage period?
[01:36] Alex: Yes, we do. The latest SOC 2 Type II covers Oct 1st 2025 through March 31st 2026. We can share the report via the Trust Center link; it's a read-only portal link we provide to customers.
[01:48] Maya: Is that the full report or a redacted version? We need the full report for our audit.
[01:52] Alex: Full report — signed. We usually require an NDA for full redistribution; we can provision access in the trust center and also send the signed copy depending on your legal team's preference.
[02:02] Sana: And ISO 27001? Certificate and statement of applicability?
[02:06] Priya: We have ISO 27001 certified covering the inference platform and control plane — I'll confirm exact in-scope systems but it's aligned with the SOC scope. So we can provide the certificate and the SoA via the trust center as well.
[02:18] Tom: For controls mapping — we need a matrix mapping Redwood controls to our HIPAA/HITRUST and ISO controls. Do you have a pre-made mapping?
[02:28] Priya: We do have a controls mapping template — common mappings for SOC/ISO to HIPAA. It's not a full attestation for specific customer implementations, but it shows which of our controls cover each requirement. We'll attach it to the trust center artifacts or drop into the shared drive.
[02:40] Alex: Quick note — sometimes the control names in our docs use internal shorthand, e.g., "KV cache" appears as K-V cash in auto transcripts, apologies for that, but the controls map will use standard nomenclature.
[02:52] Maya: Haha, yes we noticed earlier transcriptions.
[02:55] Priya: On encryption: at rest we use AES-256 with envelope encryption; customer-managed KMS is supported in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have a Redwood-managed KMS but we do offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations for an extra compliance package.
[03:12] Maya: So for Hosted, can we import keys into AWS KMS and have Redwood use them?
[03:17] Priya: Yes, in Dedicated and Private modes we support bringing your own keys (BYOK) using AWS KMS or a cloud HSM. Hosted can support CMK only in specific enterprise agreements — we'll note that as action item to clarify licensing.
[03:30] Sana: Are keys ever exported out of the KMS?
[03:33] Priya: No, keys are never exported. We use envelope encryption and the master keys remain in the customer's KMS when BYOK is enabled.
[03:40] Tom: Audit logs — retention and SIEM integration. We need 7 years retention for some artifacts and streaming to our Splunk.
[03:48] Priya: We retain control plane audit logs for 18 months by default; we can extend retention as an add-on for enterprise customers. Application-level logs — request metadata, model name, timestamps — are available in the audit exports. We also have S3-based log exports and support for streaming via Kinesis/Cloud PubSub; Splunk integration is common.
[04:05] Maya: Do logs contain any model outputs or PHI? We are sensitive to content in logs.
[04:11] Priya: By default request/response bodies are redacted from standard control plane logs. We record metadata like request id, model, token counts, latency, and whether caching occurred. For debug-only exports we can include snippets but that's gated and requires customer approval and tighter access controls.
[04:26] Alex: We should add that we offer prefix/KV cache controls — you can opt out of caching for certain routes if PHI shouldn't be cached.
[04:34] Sana: Good — we'll need that documented.
[04:36] Tom: SSO and RBAC — we use Okta today; what's the SCIM provisioning story?
[04:41] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Role-based access supports least-privilege roles and fine-grained route/model permissions. Audit trail shows who invoked which API key or user action.
[04:54] Maya: Do you offer per-token attribution back to a human user for compliance?
[04:59] Priya: We have token-level metadata and can map requests to API keys or user IDs; you can include user identifiers in headers and we store that as metadata for tracing.
[05:10] Sana: Data residency — we need data to remain in the EU for our European patients. What regions do you support?
[05:16] Priya: We have multi-region hosting and Dedicated/Private clusters can be pinned to a region. For EU-only residency, we can deploy private clusters in the EU region, and the trust center will indicate region support for artifacts.
[05:28] Maya: Any certifications for data center providers?
[05:31] Priya: We rely on cloud providers' physical security certifications — AWS/Azure/GCP — and those are listed in the trust center.
[05:39] Tom: Incident response and breach notification timelines?
[05:42] Alex: We have a documented incident response process with 72-hour notification SLA for incidents affecting customer data; that's in the security whitepaper. For severe incidents we have phone escalation.
[05:52] Maya: Okay, can you share the contact and the escalation matrix?
[05:55] Alex: Yes, we'll include the security contact and escalation matrix in the trust center bundle.
[06:00] Priya: Quick tech note — for Private deployments we can support HSM-backed keys if you need FIPS/HSM warranty.
[06:07] Sana: Great. We need to validate controls mapping against our HITRUST checklist — will Redwood help with that?
[06:13] Priya: We can provide the mapping and a short review session; we won't certify to HITRUST on your behalf, but we'll show which controls map and where you may need compensating controls.
[06:24] Tom: Any third-party pen test results or bug bounty summary we can see?
[06:29] Alex: We have recent third-party pen test summary and a bug bounty program snapshot; pen-test remediation summaries are included in the trust center. Full reports may require an NDA.
[06:39] Maya: About the trust center access flow — how do we get a read-only link?
[06:42] Alex: I'll send a Trust Center invite via email; it's role scoped. We'll provision access to Maya and Sana as read-only for compliance artifacts. That invite will include links to SOC 2, ISO, SoA, controls map, pen-test summaries, and the security whitepaper.
[06:56] Sana: Please include the KMS and encryption design doc.
[06:59] Priya: Will do.
[07:02] Alex: We're nearing the end — a few clarifying Qs: Maya, do you need the raw SOC 2 evidence or just the auditor-signed report?
[07:10] Maya: Auditor-signed report is fine for now, but we may later request selected evidence for our internal audit team under NDA.
[07:18] Priya: Noted.
[07:20] Tom: On expected timeline — when can we get the artifacts and the controls matrix?
[07:24] Alex: We can provision Trust Center access within 48 hours; full controls mapping and the KMS design doc — we'll aim for 4 business days. If you need an accelerated path we can prioritize.
[07:36] Maya: That timeline works.
[07:38] Sana: One nit — please make sure the controls matrix references exact requirement IDs; our auditors are picky.
[07:44] Priya: We'll include requirement IDs and a short glossary mapping our control IDs to standard frameworks.
[07:50] Alex: Great. Any other open concerns?
[07:53] Maya: Nothing else right now.
[07:55] Alex: OK let's recap and action items.
[08:00] Priya: Quick aside — noted a small transcript hiccup earlier where "Redwood Private" read as "Redwood Privet" in auto captions, we'll avoid that.
[08:09] Alex: Thanks everyone.
[08:12] [~end excerpt — call continued with detailed follow-ups and short Q&A; total duration ~55 minutes]
next_steps: Provision Trust Center access for Maya and Sana within 48 hours
Share signed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert via Trust Center
Deliver controls mapping (SOC/ISO -> HIPAA/HITRUST) within 4 business days
Provide KMS/encryption design doc and pen-test summaries
Schedule follow-up review session for controls mapping (optional week of 2026-05-25)
action_items: Alex Chen: Send Trust Center invite and security contact info (due 2026-05-17)
Priya Nair: Upload controls mapping, KMS design doc, and pen-test summaries to Trust Center (due 2026-05-19)
Maya Rivera: Confirm list of users to provision for Trust Center access (due 2026-05-16)
